decisions.quote: The original article states that the main analysis was a Time-Series Cross-Section Ordered Probit model. It is not clear why the decision was made to opt for the ordered probit model specifically nor how they achieved to run this model within the panel data (time-series cross-sectional model). Given the lack of this vital information about the model specification, it is unlikely that exact reproduction of this model will be possible. Given the structure of the data, the package “plm” in R was used to construct a Time-Series Cross-Section Models (i.e., not necessarily accounting for the “ordered probit”).
decisions.reason: Under the codebook for Axis 1 (outcome_computation), 'computationally reproducible' requires obtaining the original reported numbers again up to rounding or negligible numerical differences, whereas 'computational issues' applies when the analysis ran and produced numbers but the reported numbers were not obtained. Here, the analyst explicitly states that lacking vital model specification details made exact reproduction of the original Time-Series Cross-Section Ordered Probit model unlikely, substituted a linear panel pooling model in plm, and obtained N = 1,918 (vs. original 1,718, a 200-observation discrepancy) and a focal coefficient of 0.0064062 (vs. original 0.007, an ~8.5% difference that rounds to 0.006 and met only the report's 15% 'Approximate reproduction' criterion rather than 'Precise reproduction').

decisions.quote:
Analyst success criteria: For this claim, a successful reproduction attempt is a focal coefficient (the ordered probit model coefficient) within 15% accuracy of the original focal coefficient (approximate reproduction).
Reproduction outcome: Based on these criteria, the claim did reproduce.
decisions.reason: This SCORE Author Data Reproduction report performs only a single computational reproduction attempt ('Analysis attempt 1') evaluated against primary computational reproduction criteria and does not conduct robustness checks or sensitivity analyses across alternative specifications. The single reconstructed plm pooling model was the analyst's lone attempt to approximate the insufficiently documented original model, not a robustness check.
